subject: Considered alternative: structured coaching before PIP
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Performance concern — suggested next steps

Mina —

I wanted to flag an ongoing performance concern with Samir Patel (IC, Platform). Over the past two quarters his delivery velocity has slipped (missed 3/6 sprint goals), and there have been repeated production regressions tied to incomplete reviews. I captured observations in the attached workbook (mgr_observations_202503.xlsx).

Options I'm weighing:
- Start a formal PIP now (30-day timeline)
- Run a focused 30-day coaching plan with clear success criteria and manager checkpoints (less formal, gives space to improve)
- Discuss a mutual offboarding with a small severance package if there's low alignment

Before I pivot to a PIP, I wanted HR/legal input on any constraints and a template for a structured coaching plan that still preserves our ability to escalate to a PIP if there isn't improvement.

Can HR/Legal advise on recommended language and approvals needed?

Thanks,
Markus
Director, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mgr_observations_202503.xlsx

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-02T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance concern — suggested next steps

On Wed, Apr 1, 2025 at 09:12 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Mina —
> 
> I wanted to flag an ongoing performance concern with Samir Patel ...

Thanks Markus — I reviewed the observation workbook briefly. I agree we should try a structured coaching step first for two reasons: it documents efforts to support the individual and gives a reasonable chance for improvement without immediately moving to a formal PIP.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Manager-led coaching plan (30 days) using HR's coaching template (can graduate to PIP if criteria not met)
- Weekly 1:1 checkpoints documented in the observation log
- Clear success criteria (deliverables, code quality gates, review turnaround times)
- Manager to schedule kickoff with Samir by EOD Friday and share the plan with HR for record-keeping

Kimberly — can you send the coaching template and any legal caveats we need to include (confidentiality, documentation expectations)? Also advise on communication wording that preserves future options.

Mina
People Manager, Eng Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-03T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance concern — suggested next steps

Mina/Markus —

Thanks for the context and the observation workbook. Attaching a coaching-template for manager-led remediation (hr-alternative-coaching-template.docx) and a short legal safeguard checklist (legal-safeguard-checklist.pdf). Key guidance upfront:

- A documented coaching step is fine and often preferred as the first escalation. It should include objective, measurable criteria and specific examples.
- Use neutral, fact-based language in the kickoff conversation and the written plan. Avoid future-facing absolutes ("will be terminated") — instead note that failure to meet agreed criteria may result in formal performance actions, up to and including a PIP.
- Keep all notes and the observation log in our HR case file (confidential).
- If offboarding becomes the chosen route, involve Legal before any severance offer. David, see note below for termination guidance.

Timeline suggestion: 30-day coaching with weekly checkpoints; at end of 30 days we will reconvene with HR to determine next steps (close, extend coaching, or initiate PIP).

Please complete the observation log fields in the attached workbook and share the kickoff meeting invite (we will record a summary to the file).

Kimberly
HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hr-alternative-coaching-template.docx; legal-safeguard-checklist.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-04T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance concern — suggested next steps

Thanks, Kimberly. I'll schedule the kickoff with Samir today and complete the observation log by EOD Friday.

One practical question: if the coaching step fails and the individual requests voluntary separation instead of a PIP, is there a recommended severance guideline we should consider? I want to be prepared for that conversation.

-Markus

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-08T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance concern — suggested next steps

Markus —

If coaching doesn't resolve and voluntary separation is discussed, please loop Legal before any offer. Our standard practice: for ICs with under 2 years tenure, consider a single-month severance plus continuation of benefits through the end of that month; for longer tenure we have guideline ranges (see termination-checklist.pdf). We also confirm final pay and any equity vesting windows with Payroll.

I'll add the termination checklist to the HR file. For now proceed with the coaching plan and document everything — that preserves options.

David
Senior Counsel, Employment
Redwood Inference

Attachments: termination-checklist.pdf
